evidence: Owner sends to Chief, Manager and Ticket conversations now answer {conversation_id, fate:'accepted', message_id} at durable acceptance instead of waiting for started, queued or injected (Ticket t_8r4xr4q4, pull request 1338). Delivery is reported later through transcript rows and receipts under the same sender_message_id. Installed builds 11 and 12 decode fate as a String and settle every fate except refused and suppressed as sent (Outbox.swift), so a send stays visible and a later prompt_refused or prompt_uncertain row still shows its note. But most refusals now arrive after acceptance, and on those builds a refusal that arrives after the outbox settled the item as sent has no working Try Again. Following the owner rule for client-visible changes, raise MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_BUILD to 13 and set the new app build to 13. Existing HTTP admission refuses builds 11 and 12 with 426 ios_update_required before reads or actions; the existing native latch requests a TestFlight update and retains drafts and outbox work. Build 13 reads accepted, recorded, started, injected and queued as sent; uncertain and unknown fates as sent with the Delivery unconfirmed note and no resend; a refusal after acceptance reopens the item as failed with Try Again under a new sender_message_id and reconciles_sequence; a first message sent without a conversation retries into the current conversation. Additive server fields that build 13 ignores or reads as optional: pending_messages on the conversation read and waiting_messages_revision on view status. The owner-send status route now returns {outcome}; native builds do not call it. View receipts keep their kinds. The desktop shell loads the web app from home and reads no send outcome, so the desktop bridge floor stays 2. Shared Fastify injection refuses builds 9 to 12 for reads and actions with no handler run, and admits build 13. iOS host tests (ios/scripts/test-offline.sh, 242 passed) and hosted Native iOS CI (host suites and unsigned Simulator build) passed on the branch. Not tested: a signed device, TestFlight distribution, or the installed build 12 latch against this server. Matching client releases must be available for this server release; production deployment remains a later owner action. Review of staging e40325811 against the record at 8d861c5f2, the PR 1338 merge that installed iPhone build 13 was archived from (Ticket t_xpxrfjmb): the recorded digest f1010606 equals the contract digest at 8d861c5f2, and ios/ is unchanged since then. Two pull requests merged. PR 1340 changes agent documentation only. PR 1339 changes the only digest inputs: the home now accepts a Mac package only with a valid signing proof when the ZIP holds one, a preparation record saves the home revision, and the Mac update check prepares a refused package again after a newer home replaced the code that refused it (environments/updates/mac/service.ts and configuration.ts); release/published_mac_main.ts is a release-time script that no route serves. The only native surface is /api/updates machine rows. Their view contract (environments/updates/view_contracts.ts) is unchanged, so no key is added, removed or retyped. A machine row can show a new refusal detail or go from failed back to updating; build 13 decodes state and detail as String (UpdateModels.swift) and maps unknown states to its default label. The navigation view, conversation and outbox, video upload and machine routes are unchanged. The floor stays at build 13 and no change breaks it. Live check: private test-host servers from 8d861c5f2 and e40325811, each on a fresh database, received the same requests shaped like build 13 (X-Panels-iOS-Build 13 and X-Panels-Client), taken from the iOS source. 13 native reads (meta, managers, tickets, Ticket and Manager workspaces, three start-values, navigation snapshot, executor health, updates, machines, notification settings) returned 200 on both. Build 13 sends to Chief, Manager and Ticket returned fate accepted on both. Each conversation detail, view and receipts read (fate prompt) succeeded, and the view tail returned its frame on connect and again on reconnect. Navigation events and /api/changes opened as event streams. A build 13 approval decision operation was applied and its lookup returned the receipt. Video upload reserve, status and cancel returned 200, 200 and 204. All 46 records match between the servers except one value: whether the conversation view already holds the accepted message. Over three runs each, that view was empty in some runs on both servers, because acceptance answers before delivery; the key shapes otherwise match. Build 12 read, send, decision and tail requests each received 426 ios_update_required; the conversation sequence and held prompts stayed unchanged, and the Ticket stayed at needs_brief with proposal revision 1, so no refused action executed. Each server was stopped by its own PID. The probe is artifacts/build13_probe.mjs on that Ticket. Untested: the test host has no joined machines, so no live Mac machine row, signing-proof refusal or repeated preparation reached the update screen; that rests on the unchanged view contract and the String decode. No Xcode simulator, signed device or TestFlight build ran, and draft retention after 426 was not rerun because the app code is unchanged. The decision stays minimum_raised because production main still records floor 11 and this release carries the raise to 13; publish iPhone build 13 with it. The desktop bridge floor stays 2. Production deployment remains a later owner action. Review for Ticket t_crmeg86p (file catalog reads one folder per call): only server/files changed (catalog/folder.ts replaces catalog/inventory.ts, routes.ts, catalog/read.ts, catalog/config.ts, contracts.ts, logic/listing.ts). GET /api/artifact-catalog/<kind>/<id> keeps its query (directory, offset, limit) and its body {revision, directory, offset, total, entries} with entry keys key, path, label, kind, href, directory and child_count. Build 13 (ArtifactModels.swift, ArtifactListView.swift) decodes these unchanged, uses revision only to tell whether a later page of the same folder still matches, and reads childCount as a count. Two values change meaning without a type change: a folder sorts by its own modified time, and a folder that holds only empty folders now lists. Neither breaks build 13. Live check: a private test-host server on this branch with a 129,699-entry synthetic Ticket folder answered build 13 headers (X-Panels-iOS-Build 13 and X-Panels-Client) with 200 and the same body and entry keys, at the root and in a nested folder, and refused build 12 with 426 ios_update_required. The Ticket root revision also covers which linked files a folder already lists, so build 13 restarts its pages when a deep file appears or leaves, as it did when the old revision hashed the whole tree. The floor stays at build 13. Review for Ticket t_w7gvf6kv (#1345, the Chief settles Managers): only server/managers/data.ts changed for clients. set_manager_settled now asks the shared authority rule instead of requiring the owner, so the owner still passes, and PATCH /api/managers/<id>/settled keeps its body {settled} and its answer. Build 13 calls it only as the owner (RecapAPI.setManagerSettled), so nothing changes for it. Review for Ticket t_wpmrg7de (#1346, bounded Ticket detail): ticket_detail no longer returns the artifacts folder tree, in GET /api/tickets/<id> and the Ticket writes that answer with the detail. Build 13's TicketDetail (Models/TicketModels.swift) has no artifacts field and reads Ticket files from GET /api/artifact-catalog (APIClient.artifacts, TicketView), so the removed key was never decoded. The other change, in server/executor/mac/ipc/gateway.ts, is on the machine-code side and never reaches the phone. Both are reviewed by source reading against build 13. Review for Ticket t_kswn2b85 (#1347, hold messages for an offline machine): a send to a conversation whose machine is absent is now accepted and held instead of refused with HTTP 400. Build 13 reads the owner-send answer as before ({conversation_id, fate:'accepted', message_id}), so the outbox settles it as sent and shows it queued. No fate changes. The conversation read gains one optional field, machine_waiting_reason. Build 13 decodes ConversationConfiguration through fixed CodingKeys and synthesized HeldPrompt decoding, so it ignores the field and still shows 'Queued'. A refusal before acceptance now stores a cause code and its sentence in reason, instead of write_to_backend_failed. The codes are refused_before_acceptance, recipient_unavailable, machine_unavailable, conversation_save_failed, home_restarted_before_acceptance and recipient_conversation_replaced, and a send to a machine that can never join answers HTTP 400 with code machine_unavailable. Build 13's ConversationDelivery.refusalText default case turns an unknown code into words ('Not delivered · machine unavailable'), and the refusal stays retryable (Outbox.swift, ConversationModel.applyDelivery). The new build names the waiting machine on queued messages; its simulator build and host tests pass in CI. No signed device was checked. The floor stays at build 13. Review for Ticket t_3awpp4wg (Review queue as iPhone Live Activity): the server gains PUT /api/notifications/apns/live-activity, the table notification_live_activities (schema step ts_0019), and APNs liveactivity pushes from the notification loop. The route is new and only a build that has the Live Activity calls it. No existing route, body, key or type changes. The APNs sender's alert path keeps its headers and payload, and its transport code moved into one shared method. Builds 13 and older never call the new route, receive no new push, and read every existing answer as before, so the floor stays at build 13. Checked by source reading, the server tests (live_activity.test.ts, the schema step chain, the notification suites) and the host tests (244 passed). The widget extension was built and run on a Simulator, and its Lock Screen card was seen on the system Lock Screen. The Dynamic Island on the system, Apple's delivery of liveactivity pushes and push-to-start on a signed device were not checked.
